FN-84SI42H-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 98
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Allen Treadaway
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/09/2026
House Bill 98 as introduced would create the Alabama Law Enforcement Officers' Family
Scholarship Program to provide reimbursement for certain educational expenses to certain
eligible dependents of qualifying law enforcement officers. This bill would increase the
obligations of the Education Trust Fund (ETF) by an undetermined amount dependent upon the
number of eligible recipients of the scholarship, not to exceed an annual appropriation of $10
million. This bill would also create the Alabama Law Enforcement Officers' Family Scholarship
Fund in the State Treasury to receive funding for the program.
Additionally, this bill would require: (1) the scholarship amount to be capped at $3,000 for each
academic period for up to 8 semesters, or 12 quarters, in an approved postsecondary program;
and (2) the state educational benefits provided be applied only after any other financial aid has
been applied.
This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Commission on
Higher Education to administer the scholarship program and to submit an annual report to the
Legislature by January 1st. The Fiscal Year 2027 ETF appropriation proposed by the governor
includes an $8 million appropriation for this program.

Finally, this bill would create a new personalized blackout license plate with an additional
annual fee of $50, which could increase receipts to the following entities by the amounts listed
for each plate issued:
Entity Distribution
2.5% Commission to the License Plate Issuing Official $1.25
Department of Corrections $1.50
Department of Revenue Administrative Cost $1.00
Alabama Law Enforcement Officers' Family Scholarship Fund $46.25
Total $50.00

Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Representative Allen Treadaway
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/01/2026
House Bill 98 as passed the House of Representatives would create the Alabama Law
Enforcement Officers' Family Scholarship Program to provide reimbursement for certain
educational expenses to certain eligible dependents of qualifying law enforcement officers. This
bill would increase the obligations of the Education Trust Fund (ETF) by an undetermined
amount dependent upon the number of eligible recipients of the scholarship, not to exceed an
annual appropriation of $10 million. This bill would also create the Alabama Law Enforcement
Officers' Family Scholarship Fund in the State Treasury to receive funding for the program.
Additionally, this bill would require: (1) the scholarship amount to be capped at $3,000 for each
academic period for up to 8 semesters, or 12 quarters, in an approved postsecondary program;
and (2) the state educational benefits provided be applied only after all other financial aid and
proceeds from certain blackout license plates as authorized by this bill have been applied.
This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Commission on
Higher Education to administer the scholarship program and to submit an annual report to the
Legislature by January 1st. The Fiscal Year 2027 ETF appropriations bill as passed the House of
Representatives includes an $2 million appropriation for this program.

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 98
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Representative Allen Treadaway
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/01/2026
House Bill 98 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would create
the Alabama Law Enforcement Officers' Family Scholarship Program to provide reimbursement
for certain educational expenses to certain eligible dependents of qualifying law enforcement
officers and the Alabama Law Enforcement Officers' Family Scholarship Fund in the State
Treasury, to receive receipts for the program from loans, gifts, corporate sponsorships,
donations and proceeds from the sale of blackout license plates authorized pursuant to this bill.
This bill further specifies that no additional funding would be received from the Education trust
Fund.
Additionally, this bill would require: (1) the scholarship amount to be capped at $3,000 for each
academic period for up to 8 semesters, or 16 quarters, in an approved postsecondary program;
and (2) the educational benefits provided to be applied only after all other financial aid and
proceeds from certain blackout license plates authorized by this bill have been applied.
This bill would create a new personalized blackout license plate with an additional
annual fee of $50, which could increase receipts to the following entities by the amounts listed
for each plate issued:
Entity Distribution
2.5% Commission to the License Plate Issuing Official $1.25
Department of Corrections $1.50
Department of Revenue Administrative Cost $1.00
Alabama Law Enforcement Officers' Family Scholarship Fund $46.25
Total $50.00
